title: Tenant network policy shadow testing — results and incident correlation notes
content:
Summary:
We ran a targeted shadow-test campaign in three customer VPCs to validate our policy reconciliation path (policy-delta -> policy-apply -> dataplane-ack). The test surfaced two intermittent symptoms that map to recent incidents: 1) delayed policy convergence (2–12 mins) for some tenants and 2) asymmetric connectivity from customer-managed firewalls after failover. This doc captures raw evidence, hypotheses, short-term mitigations that were executed, and a runbook draft for on-call detection and immediate remediation steps.

Why we did this:
- Several customers reported transient control-plane-reachability and partial traffic drops after maintenance windows (see JIRA-INC-4521).
- We suspected policy cache TTL mismatches and edge case race during controlplane failover.
- Shadow testing lets us compare the desired policy set against what the dataplane actually received without modifying live traffic.

Environment and test design (brief):
- Shadow agent: private-agent v0.9.1 (binary run in read-only mode).
- Target clusters: corp-vpc-7, partner-site-2, regulated-onprem-3 (mixed BGP + static routes).
- Test vectors: policy-add, policy-remove, update with CIDR overlap, and policy-order change.
- Observability hooks: controlplane audit log (10s resolution), dataplane apply log (envoy/iptables), conntrack snapshots, and synthetic heartbeats routed through customer firewall (to detect asymmetric SNAT/MASQ issues).

Timeline (abridged):
- 2026-04-20 09:02 UTC: Start shadow-run against corp-vpc-7.
- 2026-04-20 09:04 UTC: First policy-add injected. Controlplane audit emitted event id cp-ev-8932.
- 09:06–09:08 UTC: Agent reports policy-delivered but dataplane apply not observed for ~3 min.
- 09:12 UTC: Dataplane applies observed for 70% of endpoints; remainder applied by 09:19.
- 09:20 UTC: Simulated node failover (drain+recreate) in partner-site-2; observed asymmetric reachability from external firewall on 2/5 nodes.
- 09:23 UTC: Oncall alerted (pager) due to synthetic heartbeats missing for regulated-onprem-3.

Symptoms observed and raw evidence pointers:
- Symptom A: Convergence lag (2–12 minutes) for a subset of policy deltas.
  - Evidence: audit -> apply timeline gaps in controlplane logs (cp-ev-8932, cp-ev-8940).
  - Dataplane logs: repeated 'policy-apply-retry' lines in node logs (private-agent debug).
  - Network traces: conntrack entries for old flows persisted across intended policy-removal (conntrack snapshots attached in GitHub PR).

- Symptom B: Asymmetric traffic through customer-managed firewall post-node-failover.
  - Evidence: external-synthetic-heartbeat failures mapped to nodes with SNAT translation from customer firewall. TCP resets observed in firewall logs; we saw flow entries with mismatched src IP expected vs observed.
  - Customer firewall configs: PBR (policy-based routing) + asymmetric SNAT rules (customer-controlled).

Initial hypotheses (ranked):
1) Stale policy index in the per-node cache + reconcilation race (high confidence):
   - Why: private-agent applies policy by diffing desired state -> local cache -> iptables/ipset. If cache update is delayed during heavy reconciliation or if the policy_delta carries overlapping CIDRs, ipset replace operations sometimes leave transient rules.
   - Evidence: timestamps on local cache writes lagging controlplane events by ~2–5s in most nodes, but some nodes showed 30–90s lag. Also saw failed ipset replace with EBUSY on one node (kernel-level lock contention).

2) Conntrack persistence preventing effective removal of old policies (medium confidence):
   - Why: conntrack holds paths for established flows; if SNAT changes or next-hop changes, firewall will drop asymmetric packets until conntrack either times out or is flushed.
   - Evidence: persistent conntrack entries with original source port/addr for up to 6 minutes. Traces show packets hitting new policy but firewall rejecting return path because SNAT mismatched.

3) Controlplane race during node failover where kube-proxy / dataplane agent runs stale reconciler order (lower confidence):
   - Why: simultaneous operations (node drain + policy rollouts) can reorder operations; e.g., iptables flush then add vs add then flush.
   - Evidence: rare logs with 'reconcile-started' followed by duplicated serial numbers in apply logs. Needs more triage.

Mitigations executed during test run (short-term):
- Roll existing shadow-run to targeted smaller delta batches (reduced concurrent deltas) — reduced observed worst-case lag window from 12m to ~3m.
- On nodes showing EBUSY ipset failure, restarted private-agent (graceful) which triggered a forced diff and immediate apply; that cleared the transient state.
- For asymmetric firewall case, instructed customer to temporarily disable PBR for test window; after disabling, synthetic heartbeats passed immediately.

Immediate runbook draft (for oncall) — quick checks and triage:
1) First 2 minutes after alert
   - Confirm scope: which tenant(s), which cluster(s) — check controlplane audit for event IDs.
   - Run: ssh to affected node(s) and run: private-agent status && sudo ipset list && sudo conntrack -L | grep <tenant-cidr>. Capture timestamps.
   - Check controlplane -> node telemetry: tail controlplane audit logs for event id.

2) If policy apply lag > 90s
   - Check for kernel-level ipset issues: dmesg for 'ip_set: ' or 'xt_set:'. If EBUSY or xt lock errors present, collect /var/log/kern.log and escalate to infra if repeated.
   - Restart private-agent on affected node(s) (graceful kill; allow agent to rehydrate cache). Note: this is a soft mitigation; use with caution for high-throughput nodes.

3) If asymmetric SNAT/failover symptoms present
   - Ask customer: are there PBR or outbound SNAT rules on the firewall? Request a temporary remove or a bypass for maintenance window.
   - If customer can't change firewall, attempt local conntrack flush for the specific flows: sudo conntrack -D -s <ip> -d <ip> --proto tcp (documented as last-resort).

4) If node failover concurrent with policy rollouts
   - Temporarily pause policy rollouts for that tenant (controlplane: pause-tenant-apply <tenant-id>) until nodes stabilize.

Notes / gotchas:
- conntrack flushes disrupt active connections; use only when customer agrees or as last-resort.
- ipset replace EBUSY seems correlated with heavy rule churn + kernel version mismatch (we saw it most on nodes running kernel 5.15.x vs 5.19.x). Consider kernel matrix audit.
- Private-agent v0.9.1 includes a log level that exposes 'cache-seq' — useful to correlate controlplane seq -> node seq. Increase log-level to debug for 10m windows only.

Permanent fixes under consideration (project proposals):
- Add a deterministic apply order and guard (apply-transaction) on private-agent so ipset replace is done with atomicity: build temp set -> swap -> cleanup. (Owner: Jules; PR open).
- Implement policy-delta backoff and micro-batching for tenants with high churn. (Owner: Product; spec in draft).
- Add per-kernel gating: detect ipset EBUSY and auto-fallback to safe-apply path which uses iptables-restore style bulk update.
- Enhance controlplane to include per-tenant 'quiet window' during node lifecycle events to avoid simultaneous drain + policy push.

Follow-ups and action items (owners + dates):
- Jules Park: finish atomic ipset apply prototype and run canary in corp-vpc-7 by 2026-05-10.
- Ethan Morales: audit kernel versions across onprem fleet and produce a matrix by 2026-04-30.
- Ariana Singh: update customer-facing runbook for conntrack flush warnings and get sign-off from legal/security on use-case by 2026-05-05.
- Priya Kapoor (me): schedule a replay + extended shadow-run with pause windows to try to reproduce the rare race by 2026-04-28.

Lessons learned (informal):
- Shadow tests are extremely valuable for uncovering interactions with customer-managed network stacks; we found multiple cases where our idealized assumptions (no PBR, symmetric SNAT) were violated.
- Small batching and a fallback apply path significantly reduce on-node contention.
- Improve signal: add the agent cache-seq to all controlplane audit events so we can more reliably compute delta -> apply latency per node.

Appendix (commands used during triage):
- private-agent status --json | jq .cache_seq
- sudo ipset list --verbose
- sudo conntrack -L | grep <tenant-cidr> | tail -n 50
- sudo journalctl -u private-agent -o short-iso --since "10 minutes ago"
- sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 | grep -i ipset

Raw evidence attachments:
- cp-ev-8932, cp-ev-8940 (controlplane audit events) — linked in 'linked_artifacts'.
- conntrack snapshots + node logs: see PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-agent/pull/203 (contains anonymized logs).

Open questions for postmortem / design review:
- Should we treat ipset replace failures as operationally-significant incidents (auto-escalate)?
- What's acceptable max convergence latency for policy deltas (SLO suggestion: P95 < 2m, P99 < 5m)?
- Do we want a per-tenant churn detector to auto-throttle applies?

Notes-to-self / rough brainstorming (leave in doc):
- Try a simulated test with high concurrency on nodes with older kernels to reproduce EBUSY quickly.
- Could NAT rewrite changes be mitigated by temporary port-preserving SNAT? Need FW change by customer — tricky.

End of doc.

(If reviewing: please add comments inline for the runbook steps that are too risky — especially conntrack flush guidance.)
